title: From Offices to Hotel Rooms: Is Conversion the Answer for Winnipeg's Older Buildings?
metaTitle: Office to Hotel Conversion: An Answer for Older Buildings?
metaDescription: In January 2026, one Winnipeg office building was slated to be a hotel. What makes a good candidate, what conversion involves and how to test feasibility.

blocks.x: Why conversion is on the table

Empty space is the starting point: CBRE put [downtown office vacancy at 17.3% in Q3 2026](https://mktgdocs.cbre.com/2299/635166d3-3766-4bba-836b-1640e9e191dc-610961676/Winnipeg_Office_Figures_Q3_202.pdf), against 18.6% at the end of 2025.

In [CBRE's January 2026 outlook](https://www.cbre.com/insights/articles/whats-ahead-for-winnipeg-commercial-real-estate-in-2026), its Winnipeg managing director said the city wasn't seeing many office conversions, pointed to one building on Broadway slated to become a hotel, and added, "that's the extent of it." So at that point, an office to hotel conversion was rare here, not a trend.

[Colliers' Q3 2026 snapshot, as reported by Wealth Professional](https://www.wealthprofessional.ca/investments/alternative-investments/ig-wealth-future-exit-could-drive-winnipeg-office-vacancy-past-19/393742), showed Class B vacancy rising from 13.8% to 19.1%. Wealth Professional tied this to IG Wealth's planned exit from 447 Portage, and said Colliers linked the jump to a reorganization of its database.

In July 2026, [IG said its move would run to mid-2028](https://www.ig.ca/en/media-room/media-releases/ig-wealth-management-strengthens-commitment-to-winnipeg-with-new-downtown-headquarters). CBRE, using its own data, put downtown Class B at 19.5% in Q3 2026.

City programs have also reached this market: the [Vacant Building Grant](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/housing/housing-accelerator-fund/vacant-building-grant), which closed to applications on August 17, 2026, accepted housing conversions from office use. It funded housing, not hotels.
Hotel conversion is a related option for owners: hotel rooms are smaller than apartments and need simpler kitchens, or none, which can make them easier to lay out in some buildings.
What makes a building a good office-to-hotel candidate
Not every office building can become a hotel. Good candidates often share several features:

Makes it easier to lay out standard room sizes
Near the convention centre, arenas, Broadway or the Exchange
Comfort, natural light and code compliance
Hotels need reliable access between floors and safe exits
Reduces the cost of major repairs

blocks.x: Deep, square office floors are harder to convert, because interior space without windows cannot easily become guest rooms.
Our view: assess before you commit

The biggest risk in a conversion is discovering a deal-breaker after the money is committed. Owners should commission a feasibility study that looks at structure, envelope, exits, accessibility, zoning and the hotel market before signing up an operator or a financing package.
A contractor's walk-through at this stage can help identify:
**Demolition scope:** how much of the existing interior must be removed.
**Envelope condition:** whether windows, masonry and doors need replacement.
**Site issues:** access, staging and noise in occupied areas.
**Phasing options:** whether floors can be converted in stages.
What a conversion involves
A typical office-to-hotel conversion includes:
**Full interior demolition** of office fit-outs, ceilings and finishes.
**Window replacement** for comfort, efficiency and acoustic performance.
**Masonry and façade repair** to update the exterior.
**New room layouts** with framing, doors and acoustic separation.
**Finishes** including flooring, paint and room doors and hardware.
**Lobby and public areas** designed for the hotel brand.
**Building systems** (mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection), with trade permits applied for by City-licensed contractors.

A change of use like this starts with a building permit application, then an [occupancy permit](/blog/occupancy-permit-change-of-use-winnipeg). In a Part 3 building, a [change in major occupancy classification](https://www.winnipeg.ca/media/6330) calls for drawings sealed by an architect or engineer. In an older building, have suspect materials [tested for asbestos](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba) before demolition starts.
The hotel operator's perspective

Hotel operators care about guest experience: quiet rooms, comfortable temperatures, good lighting and attractive public spaces. They also care about durability, because rooms are used intensively. Finish choices such as commercial-grade flooring, scrubbable paint and solid-core doors can make a real difference in long-term costs.
Existing hotels face the same expectations

Owners of existing Winnipeg hotels face the same guest expectations. Guest-room refreshes, lobby updates and window replacements can help older hotels stay competitive. Hotels can [renovate in phases](/blog/hotel-renovation-winnipeg-stay-open), floor by floor, to keep operating.
What to watch

Watch the Broadway building. If a hotel there performs well, other owners of narrow, well-located older buildings may explore hotel and residential uses. Watch also for any city or provincial incentives for conversions, which could improve project economics.
A note on costs and timelines
Conversions are complex and costs vary widely depending on the building. The largest variables are usually window replacement, building systems and the extent of demolition and structural work.

Winnipeg construction costs rose by 4% or more in 2025, according to [Altus Group's 2026 Cost Guide insights](https://www.altusgroup.com/insights/caution-in-2026-optimistic-for-2027-cost-guide-insights/), and the [Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.50%](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/10/fad-press-release-2026-10-28/) on October 28, 2026. Owners should build realistic contingencies and timelines into their feasibility studies.
Phasing a conversion, floor by floor, can allow part of the building to start earning revenue sooner, once those floors have their occupancy permit.
This is general information, not legal or financial advice.
The bottom line

Office-to-hotel conversion is not a solution for every vacant building, but for the right building it can unlock new value. Owners should assess feasibility early, involve hotel renovation contractors before they commit, and plan carefully for demolition, envelope and finishes.
